title: Why Leaves Change Color: Red and Purple

scenes.title: WHERE RED COMES FROM
scenes.caption: Some leaves make red pigments in autumn.
scenes.narration: Unlike yellow carotenoids, many red pigments become especially noticeable because trees produce them during autumn.

scenes.title: MEET ANTHOCYANINS
scenes.caption: Anthocyanins create red, purple, and crimson.
scenes.narration: Anthocyanins are water-soluble pigments. They can create vivid red, purple, and sometimes blue shades in leaves and fruits.

scenes.title: A BRIGHT AUTUMN RED
scenes.caption: Cool nights and sunny days can help.
scenes.narration: Bright days and cool nights often favor strong red colors in some species. Weather conditions influence how intense the display becomes.

scenes.title: RED IS NOT IN EVERY LEAF
scenes.caption: Some trees make more anthocyanin than others.
scenes.narration: Maples can become brilliant red, while other species turn mostly yellow or brown. Their pigment chemistry is different.

scenes.title: WHY MAKE RED PIGMENT?
scenes.caption: Scientists study several possible benefits.
scenes.narration: Anthocyanins may help protect leaves from light stress while nutrients are being recovered. Researchers continue to study their roles.

scenes.title: A COLORFUL MIX
scenes.caption: Red can combine with yellow and orange.
scenes.narration: When anthocyanins appear alongside carotenoids, leaves can show scarlet, orange-red, and purple tones across the same tree.
